That manual smoke-test command was blocked (it used command substitution, which needs approval this session doesn't support) — no action was taken. It's not needed though: `test/cli.test.js` already exercises the exact same path (spawning `src/cli.js` with `HABITS_FILE` pointed at a temp file) and all 4 of those cases passed in the full suite above.

**What changed:** `habit done <name> [date]` now accepts an optional trailing `yesterday`, `today`, or `YYYY-MM-DD` token — parsing lives in `src/cli.js` (`splitDoneArgs`), and date resolution/validation is in `src/streak.js` (`resolveDate`, UTC-safe, rejects invalid dates like `2026-02-30`). No changes to `commands.js`'s existing signature. Added 4 unit tests for `resolveDate` and 4 end-to-end CLI tests; all 15 tests pass.

One thing to be aware of: if a habit's name happens to be two+ words ending in `yesterday`/`today`/a `YYYY-MM-DD`-shaped word (e.g. `habit add "workout yesterday"`), `done` will misread that trailing word as a date instead of part of the name. This is a pre-existing ambiguity from `add`/`done` joining all args into one name — I didn't touch that behavior, just noting the edge case exists.
